sources.squareMetresASection: One section of a cover is one small hide: a moose's hide, some 3.5 m², over the three leather vanilla tans from its large hide
sources.kilogramsASquareMetre: Hide 5 mm thick (raw cowhide is 2 to 6 mm) at 860 kg/m³, dry leather (engineeringtoolbox.com)
sources.keepCelsius: Green hide keeps a day at 20 °C, two weeks at 5 °C and three weeks at 0 °C before it putrefies (CSIRO Meat Technology Update 98/3)
sources.keepQ10: From those keeping times: fourteen times longer over 15 °C colder, 5.8 times for every 10 °C
sources.raw: Untanned hide wet through putrefies as green hide does (CSIRO); once past its keeping, it rots through in as long again. Umiak skins, untanned, had to be taken out and dried daily or they rotted (indigenousboats.blogspot.com, 2011). Re-wetted fresh hide takes up some 14% of its weight within the hour (leathermag.com, soaking practices)
sources.soaked: Limed and soaked hide is still untanned collagen: no keeping time was measured for it, so it keeps as raw hide does
sources.scraped: Scraped hide is untanned collagen, as raw hide
sources.salted: Salt keeps a hide for months ashore, but soaks out of it in 8 to 20 hours afloat, as tanneries soak it out (tanning practice, 10 to 16 °C): half a day more than raw hide. Soaked cured hide takes up to 45% water (leathermag.com)
sources.oiled: Weak source: fat dressing sheds water but is no tannage, and brain- and fat-dressed hides wash out and harden when wet (leather-dictionary.com, brain tanning). An estimate of three times raw hide's keeping
sources.pelt: A pelt is an oiled hide cured with its hair on: as oiled hide. The weak source is the same
sources.prepared: Bark-tanned hide is the cured skin that survives wet burial (Tees Valley museums); Severin's oak-tanned, greased ox hides crossed the Atlantic over two summers (Brendan, 1976-77), and umiak covers lasted two to four years: a year's keeping afloat. Leather takes up to some 30% water (the water-repellent bound of US7060363)
